This site collects the reproducible analyses behind the IHC method study —
spatial single-cell IHC, bulk RNA-seq, cell-type deconvolution, clinical data,
and the image-registration / segmentation benchmarks that validate the pipeline.

The single-cell inputs come from the sibling repos: cells are segmented and
quantified by **mirage** (`../mirage`), which also phenotypes them, and gated
independently in QuPath by **FlowPath** (`../qupath-extension-flowpath`); the
benchmark tables come from mirage's `benchmarks/` sweep. `code/cell_tables.R`
reconciles the export schemas and the two phenotype vocabularies those tools
produce, so every analysis here reads one vocabulary — see `code/README.md`.

Each analysis below is a standalone page. Start with the **Overview**, then dive
into whichever thread you need. Pages marked _(in progress)_ are authored but not
yet knit to HTML, so their links may not resolve until the next site build.

## Start here

- [Overview](overview.html) — project scope, the datasets in play, and how the
  pieces fit together.

## Building the manuscript figures

- [Paper figures](paper_figures.html) — the panel assembly sheet. One panel per
  plot at publication proportions, exported as vector PDFs to
  `output/figures/paper_figures/` for assembly in Affinity, plus a named slot with
  acquisition instructions for every panel that has to be a screenshot or a
  microscope crop. Reads the all-slide export (`data/all_slide/`); knit it to see
  which panels are ready and which are still missing their input.

## Method validation & QC

The core "method" contribution: how cells are assigned to tumour annotations,
how IHC markers are quality-controlled, and how the imaging pipeline is benchmarked.

- [Annotation membership QC](annotation_membership_qc.html) _(in progress)_ —
  sf point-in-polygon membership vs. the `Out_of_annotation` flag, compared per cell.
- [IHC marker QC](ihc_qc.html) _(in progress)_ — per-marker distribution and
  bimodality checks on `ihc_data`, with no external reference.
- [Run QC](run_qc.html) — **the registration QC of the run on the study samples**:
  VALIS's or STARE's own registration error (including STARE's per-tile spatial map)
  and the independent DAPI-nucleus overlap cross-check. Reads `data/mirage/` and needs
  nothing else — the only page that renders from a pipeline run alone.

**Three pages read registration accuracy and they are not interchangeable.**
[Registration arms](registration_arms.html) is the one the manuscript needs.

- [Registration arms](registration_arms.html) — the study slides registered **once
  per configuration** (`memory_mode` high/low crossed with `reg_micro_reg` 0/1/2 =
  six arms). Ranks the arms on real tissue and separates what each knob buys. Also
  where the comparability rules live: mirage's `rigid` QC stage means affine ∘
  micro-rigid at depth ≥ 1, so it cannot be compared across depths.

The next two read mirage's `benchmarks/` **sweep**, which runs on synthetic images
to measure cost and scaling. They say nothing about your samples; Run QC does, and
the arm page does for the configuration choice.

- [Registration accuracy](registration_accuracy.html) — sweep registration accuracy:
  VALIS feature rTRE per stage, the segmentation-overlap cross-check, accuracy vs
  cost, and an agreement view of the two estimates.
- [Pipeline benchmarks](benchmarks.html) — sweep resource scaling, I/O volume,
  whole-pipeline cost and segmentation-method comparison.

## Molecular & clinical analyses

**Two clinical_data pages, one analysis.** They differ only in *who called the
phenotypes*; the slides and the pathologist polygons are the same. The choice is made
in the page's setup by `membership_data(mode, ...)` (`code/membership.R`); everything
downstream is the same document, `analysis/_clinical_data_body.Rmd`, so any difference
between the pages is attributable to that one choice.

|                | cells from | phenotypes by | membership |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clinical_data` | the all-slide export | FlowPath gate tree | region-matched polygon |
| `clinical_data_mirage` | `data/mirage/<pid>/` | **mirage's panel** | the same polygons |

Read them against each other to isolate the **phenotyping method**.

- [Clinical data](clinical_data.html) — the reference page. A cell is inside when its
  centroid falls in **that region's own** polygon (sf point-in-polygon), because the
  all-slide export pairs a cell csv with a geojson region by region. A patient with no
  annotation directory is entirely inside — the layout's own convention, marked
  `whole_slide` rather than guessed.
- [Clinical data — mirage phenotyping](clinical_data_mirage.html) — the same polygons
  and the same statistics, but the phenotypes are **mirage's own** (`panel.yaml`, no
  human in the loop) rather than the FlowPath gate tree. Reads
  `data/mirage/<patient>/`. mirage has no out-of-annotation flag and no whole-slide
  convention, so a patient without a polygon is absent rather than counted whole.

> **Two pages were removed on 2026-08-11**, `clinical_data_per_annotation` and
> `..._per_annotation_old`. They took membership from the exporter's precomputed
> `Out_of_annotation` column instead of from geometry, reading
> `data/flowpath/per_annotation/<patient>_a<k>.csv` and an `old/` overlay — a layout
> the export no longer produces, and a split that no longer exists. The current export
> ships a polygon *per region*, so geometry is available everywhere the flag used to be
> the only option.

- [Bulk RNA-seq](bulkRna.html) — DESeq2-based differential expression over the
  bulk RNA inputs.
- [Deconvolution](deconvolution.html) — cell-type deconvolution (immunedeconv),
  bridging bulk RNA (CRF-id) and IHC (patient) id spaces via the clinical table.
- [Marker exclusivity](exclusivity.html) _(in progress)_ — per-patient marker
  co-expression / lineage leakage from the whole-slide `ihc_data`.
- [Tumour border / invasive margin](periphery.html) _(in progress)_ —
  immune composition in the invasive-margin buffer around tumour annotations.
